content: The IPL auction for the 2027 season will take place on December 16 in Goa. The day-long mini-auction will be held on the same day as the second ODI between India and Sri Lanka in Bengaluru. The auction will take place nearly a month after the reten deadline, which the IPL recently informed the franchises will be November 15. Soon after that, the IPL will send the franchises the registered pool of players to shortlist from before the final list is sent out, along with the order of the sets, in the week leading into the auction. The IPL trade window has seen just two trades since the 2026 season ended. According to the IPL rules, the trade window starts a month after a season ends, stays open up to a week before the auction date, and then continues up until a month before the start of the next season. In June, Lucknow Super Giants swapped their captain Risbah Pant to Delhi Capitals (DC) in return for wristspinner Kuldeep Yadav. Recently, DC also traded fast bowler T Natarajan to Sunrisers Hyderabad for uncapped legspinner Zeeshan Ansari. The IPL has not yet finalised the dates for the 2027 season. But, in 2024, while announcing the dates for the following three seasons, it had chalked out the window between March 14 and May 30. However, in September this year, post the BCCI’s AGM, board secretary Devajit Saikia had indicated that the tournament could start in March-end. This is the last mini-auction in the IPL’s current cycle, with a mega auction scheduled ahead of the 2028 season. The next mega auction will kick-off the IPL’s next media rights cycle, though the BCCI is yet to release the tender. In 2022, the IPL joined the ivy league of global sport after the media rights were sold for an astronomical sum of INR 48,390.5 crore (US$ 6.2 billion approx.). (Cricinfo)

content: The action drama crossed the lifetime global collection of 2.0, starring Rajinikanth and Akshay Kumar, which had earned approximately Rs 691 crore during its theatrical run. On Sunday, October 25, Jailer 2 took its worldwide gross collection to Rs 710.35 crore, according to trade tracker Sacnilk. The film’s latest milestone comes 11 days after its theatrical release on October 15. With this achievement, Jailer 2 has also emerged as the highest-grossing Tamil film of 2026. At the domestic box office, Jailer 2 recorded a gross collection of Rs 25.70 crore on Sunday. Its total India gross now stands at Rs 466.85 crore, while its India nett collection has reached Rs 398.70 crore. According to Sacnilk, the Tamil version contributed Rs 17.35 crore on Day 11 from 5,683 shows. The Telugu version added Rs 4.50 crore across 1,860 shows, while the Hindi version collected Rs 3.15 crore from 4,195 shows. The Kannada version contributed another Rs 0.70 crore from 216 shows. The film’s strong performance across multiple language versions has helped it maintain its box office momentum and achieve the worldwide record. Jailer 2 Sets Multiple Box Office Records Besides overtaking 2.0 to claim the top spot among Tamil films worldwide, Jailer 2 had already registered several milestones during its opening days. The film became the fastest Tamil release to cross the Rs 300 crore and Rs 400 crore marks in worldwide collections, achieving the former within three days and the latter on Day 4. The latest achievement further strengthens Rajinikanth’s position as one of Tamil cinema’s biggest box office draws. Director Nelson Dilipkumar also reacted to the film’s performance in theatres. Celebrating the audience response, he wrote on X, “Theatres are going bonkers! Thalaivar magic hits different. Thank you, dear audience, for the phenomenal love and reception for #Jailer2. Nothing beats seeing the audience celebrate it like this! Thank you all for the love and support. @rajinikanth sir @anirudhofficial @sunpictures.” Background Bankrolled by Sun Pictures, Jailer 2 features a large ensemble cast alongside Rajinikanth. The film stars Ramya Krishnan, Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar, Jackie Shroff, Yogi Babu, Mirnaa, Rithvik, S. J. Suryah, Vidya Balan, Suraj Venjaramoodu, Mithun Chakraborty, Hrithik Roshan, Vijay Sethupathi, Jatin Sarna, Namo Narayana, Hakkim Shahjahan and Kottayam Nazeer. (NDTV)

The warning issued by the National Building Research Institute (NBRI) will remain in effect until 2:45 p.m. tomorrow (Oct. 27). Additionally, Level 2 (Amber) and Level 1 (Yellow) landslide warnings have been issued for several other Divisional Secretariat divisions. content: The United States Navy ship USS Canberra (LCS-30) arrived at the Port of Colombo this morning, 26 October 2026 for replenishment purposes. content: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after more than 10 months in exile. “I am here. With you,” Machado wrote on X on Sunday. Her return comes after repeated prior efforts to re-enter the country came to no avail. In January, a month after Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat under cover of darkness to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, the US seized her opponent, President Nicolás Maduro. The Trump administration then backed his deputy, Delcy Rodríguez, as leader and she was sworn in as interim president, later signing an oil deal which granted very favourable terms to the US. Machado was photographed on Sunday attending Mass at a church in the Venezuelan state of Lara, surrounded by supporters hugging her and clasping her hands. She then began travelling to the capital Caracas in a caravan of cheering supporters. More supporters have lined the route of her journey to the capital. She was photographed smiling as she leaned out of the sunroof of a car as she entered Caracas late on Sunday night. “Night of reunion in our Caracas. For the reunion of each family, for the Freedom of each political prisoner, for the Freedom of Venezuela,” she wrote on X. Her ally, former presidential candidate Edmundo González, confirmed her arrival, writing in a statement: “I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil.” “Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!” González said. He added that he will soon join Machado in Venezuela to advance the country “toward freedom”. An advisor to Machado said in September that over the previous few weeks Machado had attempted seven times to return to Venezuela, but was denied each time. There have been reports that the US was involved in delaying her return, which it has denied. It’s unclear what Machado plans to do next now that she’s back, but she has previously said she would run for president again if an election were held . Her ability to return to her country was always contingent on approval from the Trump administration, which it appears has now been granted. A staunch supporter of democracy, Machado won an independent presidential primary election – held outside the Maduro government’s official election authority – in 2023, earning more than 90% of the vote. Despite winning the primary, Maduro’s government barred Machado from running for office, accusing her of fraud and tax violations. Machado denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated. She spent her final days in the country hiding in safehouses before her fleeing to Norway to accept the Nobel Prize. In the 2024 election, Machado’s ally González ran in her place against Maduro. The electoral authority, which is closely aligned with the government, declared Maduro the winner without making detailed voting tallies public. The opposition argued that González won the election, not Maduro, uploading copies of the voting tallies as evidence. Maduro was removed from the country by US forces in January, and is currently jailed in New York where he faces drugs, weapons and torture charges. He has pleaded not guilty. A spokesman for Machado called her return “a major step toward a democratic transition and free, fair, and verifiable presidential elections in the near future”. “We thank President Donald Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the US Government, Congress, and allied governments for their continued leadership and support,” her spokesperson, David Smolansky, added. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump said, “I don’t know anything about” her return, and added that he hoped she was “safe”. “I think she’s a very nice woman. The committee that issues the prize had said “it cannot be revoked, shared, or transferred to others”. He added: “We expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy.” BBC The post Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile appeared first on DailyNews .

content: Warning for strong winds and rough seas Issued by the Natural Hazards Early Warning Centreaa Issued at 09.30 a.m. 26 October 2026, valid for the next 12 hours The Deep Depression over the East-central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal has intensified into cyclonic storm “Arnab”. It has moved westwards and lay centered at 5.30 a.m. of today, the 26th October, 2026, near Latitude 15.4°N and Longitude 88.9°E. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards, and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over west central Bay of Bengal by 1800 UTC of 26th October and into a very severe cyclonic storm over the same region on 27th October. Wind speeds in the sea areas marked under the “Warning” category may increase to 80-100 kmph at times, heavy thundershowers can occur, the wave height may increase about (3.0 –4.0) meters in the mentioned sea areas and the sea conditions in these areas will become very rough. Therefore, Naval and fishing communities are warned not to venture to the sea areas bounded by 10N to 20N latitude and 80E to 95E longitude until further notice. Naval and fishing communities operating in those sea areas are advised to move away from the affected sea areas.

content:
U.S. Ambassador Eric Meyer today presented a master’s degree from the U.S. Naval Postgraduate School (NPS) to Lieutenant Commander Piyumi Kathriarachchi of the Sri Lanka Navy at the American Center Colombo. The ceremony was also attended by Rear Admiral Rohan Joseph, Director General of Training, and Commander C.R.P. Walakuluge, Director of Media, Sri Lanka Navy.

“Lieutenant Commander Kathriarachchi’s achievements reflect both her exceptional dedication and the value of world-class American military education. Through U.S.-funded training, she has gained knowledge and skills that she is now bringing home to strengthen Sri Lanka’s Navy. Her success demonstrates how investing in the professional development of our partners strengthens our defense cooperation and contributes to a safer, more secure Indian Ocean region,” said U.S. Ambassador Eric Meyer.

LCDR Kathriarachchi graduated near the top of her class at the U.S. Naval Postgraduate School (NPS), a graduate university in Monterey, California, that prepares military and defense professionals for leadership roles.

She completed the Defense Logistics Management program with honors, earning a 3.98 grade point average (GPA) out of a possible 4.0—nearly a perfect score. She also received the NPS Outstanding Thesis Award and the Kiwanis Club of Monterey Outstanding International Student Award, which the club gives to only two NPS international students each year.

Her studies were funded by the U.S. International Military Education and Training (IMET) program, which helps Sri Lankan military personnel develop skills and expertise they can bring home to strengthen their services and deepen defense cooperation between the United States and Sri Lanka.

LCDR Kathriarachchi’s award-winning research on spare parts procurement challenges facing the Sri Lanka Navy demonstrates how U.S. military education equips Sri Lankan officers with practical expertise they can apply at home, strengthening naval readiness and our bilateral defense partnership.

Reflecting on her studies in the United States, she said, “My time in the United States gave me new tools to tackle real challenges facing our Navy. I look forward to putting that knowledge to work in service of Sri Lanka and hope my experience encourages other young Sri Lankans to pursue opportunities that can make a difference for our country.”

A graduate of Taxila Central College in Horana, LCDR Kathriarachchi has a history of breaking barriers, becoming the first female midshipman in Sri Lanka Navy history to receive the prestigious Sword of Honour in 2013.

මේ සම්බන්ධයෙන් ඉදිරියේදී ඇති වන ඕනෑම සැලකිය යුතු වර්ධනයක් වහාම අනාවරණය කිරීමට කටයුතු කරනු ලබන බව LAUGFS Gas PLC විසින් කොළඹ කොටස් වෙළෙඳපොළ වෙත වැඩිදුරටත් දැනුම් දී ඇත.

හම්බන්තොට ජාත්‍යන්තර වරාය පරිශ්‍රයේ පිහිටි මෙට්‍රික් ටොන් 30,000ක ධාරිතාවයකින් යුත් LPG හෙවත් ද්‍රවීකෘත පෙට්‍රෝලියම් ගෑස් පර්යන්තයේ අයිතිය LAUGFS Terminals Limited සතුව පවතින අතර, එහි මෙහෙයුම් කටයුතු ද එම සමාගම විසින් සිදු කරනු ලැබේ.

summary_en: A formal visit to Sri Lanka was commenced on 26 October 2026 by INS Tir, INS Sujata and ICGS Sarathi of the Indian Navy’s First Training Squadron, with 135 officer under-trainees participating across the three vessels. The ships were welcomed by the Sri Lanka Navy in accordance with time-honoured naval traditions. Bilateral ties, mutual cooperation and professional knowledge-sharing are expected to be strengthened through programmes organised during the visit.

content:
A formal visit to Sri Lanka was commenced today, 26 October 2026, with the arrival of three (3) ships belonging to the Indian Navy’s First Training Squadron (1TS)—INS Tir, INS Sujata and ICGS Sarathi. The visiting ships were welcomed by the Sri Lanka Navy in accordance with time-honoured naval traditions.

Participation in the visit across the three vessels is being undertaken by a total of 135 officer under-trainees. INS Tir, a 107m-long Training Ship, is commanded by Captain Tijo K Joseph. INS Sujata, a 103m-long Offshore Patrol Vessel, is commanded by Commander Jishnu Madhavan, while ICGS Sarathi, a 105m-long Offshore Patrol Vessel, is commanded by Commandant Kundan Singh.

Meanwhile, a call on the Commander Western Naval Area, Rear Admiral Harsha De Silva, was made today by the Commanding Officers of the visiting ships at the Western Naval Command Headquarters. Mementoes were also exchanged between them, signifying the importance of the occasion.

During their stay in the country, participation by the crews and officer under-trainees is scheduled in programmes organised by the Sri Lanka Navy to foster bilateral ties and mutual cooperation. Personnel of the Sri Lanka Navy will also be provided with the opportunity to visit the training operations aboard the vessels and exchange professional expertise. In addition, several key locations and places of interest across the island are expected to be toured by the visiting personnel during their visit.

content: LAUGFS Gas PLC has officially informed shareholders and the Colombo Stock Exchange that it is engaging in preliminary, informal discussions regarding strategic options for its wholly owned subsidiary, LAUGFS Terminals Limited. LAUGFS Terminals Limited owns and operates a 30,000 MT liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) terminal situated at the Hambantota International Port. In a corporate disclosure submitted to Colombo Stock Exchange today (26) the company confirmed it is holding exploratory talks with interested parties. The options currently under evaluation include commercial collaboration, securing outside investment, or the potential disposal of part or all of LAUGFS Gas PLC’s shareholding in the subsidiary. The company highlighted that no agreement has been reached concerning the structure or terms of any prospective transaction, and no definitive agreement has been executed. LAUGFS Gas PLC noted that there is no assurance these preliminary discussions will result in a finalized deal, meaning any financial impact cannot be determined at present. LAUGFS Gas PLC stated that it will promptly disclose any material developments as required by the Listing Rules of the Colombo Stock Exchange.

headline_en: iDealz Unveils Latest iPhone 18 at HELLO18

summary_en: The iPhone 18 was officially introduced to the Sri Lankan market by iDealz Lanka (Pvt) Ltd at the HELLO18 launch event held recently in Colombo. An Experience Zone was provided for customers and technology enthusiasts to test the new devices and gain a practical understanding of their features. The launch was positioned as part of the company’s commitment to accessible, informative and engaging technology marketing.

content:
The iPhone 18 model was officially introduced to the market by iDealz Lanka (Pvt) Ltd at an event held recently in Colombo. The event was attended by a large gathering that included technology enthusiasts and customers.

The official unveiling of the iPhone 18 model was presented as the principal feature of the event. In addition to the presentation, through which particular attention was directed towards the new devices, a dedicated Experience Zone was arranged to allow customers to test the devices in person. Attendees were thereby provided with an opportunity to examine the device range closely and gain a clear understanding of the products through practical use.

The launch was presented as extending beyond the introduction of a product to the market, with customers being enabled to experience the technology and make informed purchasing decisions. A broader shift taking place in modern technology marketing was reflected through this approach.

By enabling customers to experience the new devices directly, iDealz’s commitment to bringing modern technology closer to consumers and further strengthening the trusted relationship between the brand and its customers was demonstrated.

Comments were made by iDealz Lanka (Pvt) Ltd Founder and Chairman Mohamed Rifkan: “Technology can be understood better when customers are given an opportunity to experience it for themselves. Through HELLO18, our objective was not limited to introducing a new range of devices, but was also focused on creating a genuine experience through which customers could be brought closer to technology. Meaningful customer communication conducted through well-informed guidance is believed by us to be an essential component of modern technology marketing.”

iDealz has been established as a recognised name within Sri Lanka’s mobile and technology retail sector, while smartphones and related devices are continuously made available to customers through its showrooms and digital channels. The company’s continued commitment to customer communication, together with its focus on delivering an accessible, informative and engaging technology marketing experience, was reflected through the HELLO18 launch.

headline_en: Independent Probe Ordered into Homagama Police Custody Death
headline_si: හෝමාගම පොලිස් භාරයේදී පුද්ගලයකු මියයාම සම්බන්ධයෙන් ස්වාධීන විමර්ශනයක් නියෝග කෙරේ
summary_en: An urgent and independent investigation has been ordered into the reported death of a person held in the custody of the Homagama Police. content: Sri Lanka’s total exports have reached US$ 13.61 Bn during the first nine months of 2026, recording a year-on-year growth of 5.04% compared with US$ 12.96 Bn in the corresponding period of 2025. This positive performance reflects the continued expansion of the country’s export sector, supported by growth in both merchandise and services exports. According to the latest export performance figures released by Sri Lanka Customs, together with the EDB’s estimates for gems and jewellery and petroleum products, merchandise exports grew by 5.35% to US$ 10.76 Bn during January–September 2026, compared with US$ 10.22 Bn recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. Meanwhile, services exports grew by 3.88% to US$ 2.85 Bn, up from US$ 2.74 Bn in the corresponding period of the previous year. The performance of both segments highlights the importance of strengthening Sri Lanka’s export competitiveness while diversifying its sources of export earnings. Strong Export Performance in September 2026 Sri Lanka recorded a particularly strong performance in September 2026, with total exports reaching US$ 1.69 Bn, an impressive year-on-year increase of 17.23% compared with US$ 1.44 Bn in September 2025. Merchandise exports were the main driver of this monthly growth, increasing by 21.66% to US$ 1.39 Bn, compared with US$ 1.14 Bn in September 2025. Services exports also recorded a positive performance, rising by 0.67% to US$ 306.17 Mn from US$ 304.14 Mn in the corresponding month last year. The strong growth in merchandise exports during September contributed significantly to the overall improvement in export earnings, reinforcing the positive trajectory of Sri Lanka’s export sector. Sustaining Export Growth Towards National Targets The export performance achieved during the first nine months of 2026 represents continued progress towards strengthening Sri Lanka’s position in international markets and expanding its contribution to the national economy. Sustaining this momentum will require continued efforts to diversify export products and markets, enhance value addition, improve product quality and standards, and strengthen the competitiveness of Sri Lankan exporters. The National Export Development Plan (NEDP) 2026–2030, which targets US$ 36 Bn in annual export earnings by 2030, provides a strategic framework for accelerating export growth through improved trade facilitation, market development, investment promotion, innovation, and enhanced private-sector engagement. Building on the positive results recorded in the first nine months of 2026, continued coordination among government institutions, industry stakeholders, and exporters will be essential to maintaining growth, addressing emerging challenges, and realising Sri Lanka’s long-term export development ambitions. content:
By Jithendra Antonio. Great-power competition has been presented as an opportunity through which US$10 billion in foreign investment could be attracted to Sri Lanka and the country could be established as an economic bridge between India, China, the Gulf, the USA and the West. From Trincomalee’s energy reserves and Colombo’s maritime gateway to Hambantota’s industrial potential and Mannar’s renewable-energy frontier, an opportunity has been identified for Sri Lanka’s geography to be transformed into economic power. The central challenge has been defined as the attraction of capital from competing powers without the freedom to determine the country’s own future being surrendered.

A warning regarding the emerging Indian Ocean order was issued through an assessment by Indian Ocean strategist Keerthi Martyn. In June 2026, a fresh round of scrutiny was applied to Indian Ocean security when “Navigating the Currents: Sri Lanka’s National Security Debate in the New Indian Ocean Order” was published by Martyn through the Observer Research Foundation and was subsequently republished by the Center for a New American Security. The publication was made available at https://www.orfonline.org/public/uploads/upload/20260623112717.pdf.

An uncomfortable question was raised for Colombo through Martyn’s assessment: “Can Sri Lanka preserve its freedom of action when its location, infrastructure and economic vulnerabilities make it increasingly important to larger powers?”

A striking geographical observation was presented at the opening of the chapter. Sri Lanka was described as being located at the crossroads of the Indian Ocean, approximately 10 nautical miles from major sea lanes through which a substantial share of global energy and container traffic is carried. It was argued by Martyn that the island is made both a significant maritime actor and a focus of strategic competition by this location.

Intensifying US–China rivalry, China’s infrastructure investments, American maritime-security partnerships and India’s growing influence over Sri Lanka’s security and defence decisions were identified as central pressures by which the island’s choices are being shaped.

A previous article written by Jithendra Antonio on January 27, 2025, and widely published under the title “Sri Lanka’s Maritime Revolution: Must-Do Strategy to Unlock Global Trade Power from Heart of Indian Ocean,” was also cited in the opening passage as a reference supporting the strategic significance of Sri Lanka’s location. Through the citation, the island’s maritime potential was placed within a wider debate concerning national security and international competition.

Martyn’s argument was extended beyond geography. Risks arising from domestic governance weaknesses, limited maritime capabilities, inadequate preparedness for supply-chain disruptions and difficulties in maintaining strategic flexibility amid competition among external powers were highlighted in the assessment.

From Trincomalee’s energy reserves and Colombo’s maritime gateway to Hambantota’s industrial potential and Mannar’s renewable-energy frontier, an opportunity has been identified for Sri Lanka’s geography to be transformed into economic power. The central challenge has been defined as the attraction of capital from competing powers without the freedom to determine the country’s own future being surrendered.

A warning regarding the emerging Indian Ocean order was issued through an assessment by Indian Ocean strategist Keerthi Martyn. In June 2026, a fresh round of scrutiny was applied to Indian Ocean security when “Navigating the Currents: Sri Lanka’s National Security Debate in the New Indian Ocean Order” was published by Martyn through the Observer Research Foundation and was subsequently republished by the Center for a New American Security. An uncomfortable question was raised for Colombo through Martyn’s assessment: “Can Sri Lanka preserve its freedom of action when its location, infrastructure and economic vulnerabilities make it increasingly important to larger powers?”

It was argued by Martyn that the island is made both a significant maritime actor and a focus of strategic competition by this location.

Intensifying US–China rivalry, China’s infrastructure investments, American maritime-security partnerships and India’s growing influence over Sri Lanka’s security and defence decisions were identified as central pressures by which the island’s choices are being shaped.

A previous article written by Jithendra Antonio on January 27, 2025, and widely published under the title “Sri Lanka’s Maritime Revolution: Must-Do Strategy to Unlock Global Trade Power from Heart of Indian Ocean,” was also cited in the opening passage as a reference supporting the strategic significance of Sri Lanka’s location. Through the citation, the island’s maritime potential was placed within a wider debate concerning national security and international competition.

Martyn’s argument was extended beyond geography.
